messages.text: Roads okay your way? Heard there were extra patrol cars by Athol this afternoon.
I came through slow. One stopped me for 42 in that 35 stretch and let me go with a written warning.
Lucky. You were probably polite as ever.
He was courteous too. I did look at the slip when I got home so I know where it says what happened.
I found the February receipts and that Blue Cross envelope on the washer. Want them left there?
Please put them on the kitchen table by the calculator. I still need to match them with the March list before I take the envelope to Elaine.
I am changing sheets in the back room before Linda maybe comes through Friday. Can you bring the folding cot in from the shop?
I can. That room still has your yarn boxes in front of the closet.
Same blue sleeve as last year?
Yes, the blue sleeve with the bank statement copies tucked behind it.
I will move them. Also remind me not to buy those little chew sticks Marlene mentioned for the church basket. We have nowhere to use them here.
Fine by me. Fewer things on the grocery list.
Coffee Friday still good? Also did you ever sort out that over-65 sheet from the clinic?
Friday works. I kept the sheet and marked the questions for Dr. Whitcomb before I let Leonard talk himself out of anything.
That sounds like you. Bring it along and we can compare notes while the coffee is hot.
I put your blue mug by the coffee pot for after the pantry sorting. Joan said she may bring those library notes by if she sees you.
Thank you. I will come early enough to wipe the fellowship tables, then I need to head home before it turns into an all-day thing.
That sounds right. We can sit ten minutes in the kitchen afterward and catch up without adding anything else to your day.
Could you bring the green ledger Sunday? I have two little receipts from the supper table that need tucking in before Monday.
Yes. I will put it with the hymn folder so I do not walk off without it.
For Thursday supper, do you want me to put you down for a pot of that orange soup you brought last fall?
Yes, I still have my note from the last batch with the nutmeg marked down. I will make it Wednesday afternoon.
Thank you. Also, if you have one jar of that blackberry left, the ladies asked about putting a few jars beside the coffee urn.
I have three small jars. I will label them tonight and bring the receipt slips in the same bag.
Good. If you have a spare copy of those notes someday, my girls would use them too.
I am trying to clean them up for Melanie, Brian, and the little ones, but my handwriting is a project by itself.
Kids' school auction is Saturday. They put our table near the side patio, so I asked for seats away from the door.
Thank you. I do better away from that patio crowd. Water or coffee is plenty for me.
Got it. I also told Lisa not to buy you one of those little sealed tins from the raffle table.
Good thinking. I would just bring it back home unopened and feel silly.
Roads look clear Saturday. If the kids' coughs stay gone, we could come after lunch.
That would suit us. I have Caleb's card ready and Maddie's hat only needs the last row.
They'll like that. Can you text Sara the oven time for the apple thing?
I will send it to her. Leonard can check the driveway in the morning before you leave Spokane.
Coffee at Miller's still good for 10? I can park close if the steps by the side door are icy.
Yes, close parking would help. My fingers are slow this morning too, so I am bringing the scarf but only for a few rows.
Bring it. We can talk more than stitch, and I will open the creamers if those little lids act stubborn.
Mom, I sent the clinic picnic pictures in the family thread. You might have to tap the little camera-colored icon to see all four.
I saw the first one after your father showed me where it landed. I don't open that icon unless someone tells me there is something waiting.
That is probably healthier than reading the county commission argument under the article.
I read enough to know people were wound up, then closed it before my fingers got ideas.
Mom, did you get the county sample ballot yet? The clinic break room has been arguing about those commissioner names all afternoon.
It came today. I put a check by the one who answered plainly about keeping the levy down and letting the county handle its own roads.
That sounds like you. What about the clerk race?
I may mark Sara Bell there. I know how she handled those records at the clinic office, and that matters more to me than the column she filed under.
Loose step by the porch is worse than I thought. Need anything from the shed before I pull the toolbox out?
Just the small receipt box from the shelf. I am finishing the March envelope after the soup goes in the freezer.
Got it. I will roll the bins back after I eat and then look at that step.
Thank you. If Dr. Keller's office calls while you are outside, I wrote the new time beside the phone.
Mom, when you look at Dad's clinic paper, make sure the Medicare line did not get counted twice.
I will. I had $4,200 penciled in before those lines, and then I took off the drug plan and the little tax bite.
That sounds like the right order. If the bank page shows the same three credits as last month, the bill is probably the only odd thing.
Yes, two came early in the week and Leonard's showed this morning. The interest was barely worth writing down, but I did.
Morning. If you see anything from the Spirit Lake road folks, can you tell me how 41 looks? We may try coming over after lunch.
I will look when I do my first check. Yesterday they were saying slush near the curves by town, but I have not looked today.
Thanks. I sent a picture of the kids from pajama day too, in case it gets buried under all your library and garden notices.
I saw it just now. Good picture. The library note says story hour moved to 10, and the seed people are still arguing about starting tomatoes too early.
Mom, kids have practice Tuesday. You and Dad still heading into town that morning?
If the roads are clear, yes. I want to stop by the school gym before picking up eggs.
Forecast says sun by ten. Watch that shady patch by the feed store.
I will. The little county sheet is already in my purse so I don't stand there guessing.
Kids are asking if Grandma has any of that yellow bread left if we stop by after errands.
I can put a pan in. There is also bean soup enough for bowls, and sliced apples if they want something before you drive back.
Kids are asking if Grandma will come watch them at the school field when we visit tomorrow.
I can walk around the outside path with them once if they keep my pace. Then I will be happy on the bleachers.
That works. We will not need much, just something simple before the road.
That works. They mostly want to show you their new shoes anyway.
I will keep Leonard from cutting a big piece of the roast. The little ones can have bread and soup first.
Good. I will save my knees for getting the peas tucked in after lunch.
Leaving in a few minutes if the sidewalk is not slick. I should be back before seven.
Foggy down by the water. Take the yellow jacket.
I will. Just doing the usual loop and not hurrying.
Coffee is on.
I am stopping at Yoke's before I come home. Need napkins, coffee, and two packs of paper plates for Thursday, but I am keeping it under the envelope amount.
Get the sturdy plates. Last time the thin ones folded under gravy.
I wrote that on the list. Also moving the sign-in clipboard by the door so folks do not crowd the serving table.
I can unload the bags when you pull in. Same back shelf as always?
Are you two still looking at Sun Valley, or did Leonard talk himself into staying home?
Still looking. I told him two nights is plenty if the little envelope catches up.
That sounds like you. I would add a day, but I know you would think about it the whole drive back.
Exactly. I want to enjoy it, not count what every extra morning costs.
I have looked at the luncheon table notes twice already and keep adding little things. Could you take the centerpieces off my hands?
Yes. I will bring the jars and ribbon Wednesday. You leave the bin on the porch and do not sort it again.
Thank you. I am going to walk down to the church mailbox before I start moving everything around again.
Good. Say your prayer on the way and let Wednesday be Wednesday.
Roads were decent today. Kids asked if the little path down by the water is too muddy for boots yet.
Muddy by the bottom step, but the upper path is fine. Tell them to come early if they want to hear the red-winged ones before everyone starts up their saws.
Mom, do you still keep old paperwork from when the house got signed over clear? My scanner at work can do a stack if you want.
Thank you, honey. The deed papers and the car titles are already in the fire box. I only need the March Visa slip filed after I send the full amount on the 12th.
I can bring the loppers. That blowdown near the shed looked close last time.
Got it. Also if that county packet asks for copies, just bring whatever monthly letters you actually get.
Thank you. We will trim what has to be trimmed and leave the rest for cover. Your dad says the old mill men would laugh at me measuring branches.
That should be a short pile. Just the retirement deposits, Leonard's pension note, and the tax receipt from the county.
We can come by after lunch Saturday if the roads stay dry. Need anything from Spokane?
No, thank you. I filled the Sunday tray this morning and we are set until the Rite Aid stop later in the month.
Got it. Kids can walk the block with you if you want to stretch your legs.
That would be nice. I will do a plain chicken soup, not too salty, and keep my good shoes by the door.
I put the North Idaho Heating paper in the blue folder. The February page still looks ugly at $3,400.
That blower motor better behave for ten years.
I am leaving the March grocery and house lines where they were, around $2,800 unless the car complains.
Car is fine. I will skip the hardware store unless we actually need something.
Shop says the water heater part may run close to $400 if they cannot clean the old one.
All right. Let him confirm before we move anything from the side account.
He is checking now. I told him no rush until he knows.
If it has to be done, we can put it back $50 at a time after the checks land.
If I come through Spirit Lake Friday, do you want coffee before noon? Sandpoint got slush again this morning.
Friday works if the hill by Careywood is clear. I am already making one town list, so I can get the canning lids and oatmeal while we are out.
Good. I will check the plow report before I leave and bring those old photos from Mom's kitchen box.
That would be nice. If it turns slick, stay here overnight and we will not fuss with the drive back.
Did you ever find that blue rubber bottle from Mom's linen closet?
Found it behind the towels. I filled it after dishes and made a mug with honey, then kept shaving edges off the apple pan while it cooled.
That sounds like our kitchen growing up. Put the pan away before you even it clear to the other side.
Too late for one corner, but I wrapped the rest for coffee Wednesday.
Do you want me to bring the muffin pan back before Tuesday, or leave it on your porch after prayer group?
Tuesday is fine. Leonard and I will be here after lunch unless he talks me into the Co-op run.
I will come by then. I still smile at that old photo on your hall table with Leonard's wide tie.
That tie was something. The frame is getting loose, so I set it by the 1984 album to fix later.
Do you still want my leftover blank envelopes for Tuesday? I found a full stack in the church office cabinet.
Yes, please. The ladies used nearly all the pink ones last week, and I have three soft hats ready to tuck into the center basket.
I can bring them after choir practice. Do you need me to help move chairs again?
If you have a minute, yes. I want the tables close enough that Mrs. Evers can reach the scissors without getting up.
I should be home by 2:30 if that still works. The last patient chart took longer than expected.
That works. Leonard is outside anyway, and I want to hear how things are up there before I call Brian back.
Perfect. I also found the billing code you asked about, so keep the paper handy.
I will. I set Brian's envelope beside yours so I do not mix up the photos.
Mom, when you fill out that clinic update, you can leave the employer box alone if nothing has changed. They mostly need Leonard's med list and your usual household numbers.
Thank you. I was looking at it after church and did not want to put the senior center and library hours in the wrong spot.
Those sound like community hours, not anything for that box. Just note the days you are usually out of the house if they ask about availability for appointments.
That helps. This week is Tuesday morning at the center, Thursday shelves, and Saturday setup for the lunch.
Kids' spring concert got moved to Thursday night. If you come over, don't rush after your center morning.
Thursday is just soup labels and name tags this time. I put Carol beside those on the list, so I can leave by noon if needed.
Good. Let somebody else carry a clipboard once in a while.
I am practicing. I already told Ruth I would bring two pies for Memorial Day, but my name is not going on the top sheet.
Dad said you two might be headed this way Friday. Roads by Deer Park were wet but clear today.
Thank you. I wrote the time on the kitchen calendar, but I still need to put the morning buzz in my phone so we do not dawdle over breakfast.
Need me to print anything if the office sends it late?
Maybe. I have his blue folder started with the old sheet and the little list from the pillbox lid.
I got the living room lamp on. KREM starts in a bit.
Good. I am warming the soup and will bring your cushion in before the first segment.
Leave your phone by the bread box after. You slept better last time you read instead of scrolling.
I put the bookmark in the blue mystery. That will be enough for tonight.
I am leaving Sandpoint after the bank opens. If 95 looks worse by Athol I may just come on in and wait it out.
That is fine. I changed the sheets in the small room after church things yesterday, and there is soup enough for two bowls.
Good. I put Carl's envelope in my purse too, so remind me before I forget.
I will. We can look at those old pictures while the roads settle down.
Are you still stopping at the library before coffee? I can bring that blue flyer they handed out in Sandpoint.
Yes. I want to compare it with ours before the meeting. Ours mentions shorter hours again and that roof patch.
I also saw the senior van schedule changed. Tuesday medical runs are full already.
That is the kind of thing I want them to keep plain on the sheet. If people can use it, I do not mind paying attention to the details.
Do you want coffee before the Tuesday library table, or would that crowd the afternoon?
Let's just do coffee at your kitchen after lunch. I want to reread the courthouse chapter before I go.
That sounds easier. I will save you one muffin and you can show me the note card you mentioned.
Thank you. I only have three questions written down, so I should still be home before Leonard starts the news.
The clinic paper came with two $24 lines and one $9 line. I set it beside the little March sheets before I do anything with it.
Send me a picture of the top half when you can. Sometimes they list the adjustment and the patient part on separate rows.
I will. I already wrote the $9 on the refill page, but I did not touch the teeth/eyes page until you look.
Good. If it is duplicated, wait for the corrected copy before you move money around.
Sun is out. I scraped the windshield.
Good. I'll bring my reading glasses and the county card from the fridge.
We can park by the side door at the gym, then groceries.
That works. I would rather handle the paper there when it is this nice out.
I left the hose by the back steps. Sun is off that patch now.
Thank you. I will do the lettuce and onion strips after supper while it is cooler.
Saw your little book on the porch rail. Wind was picking up if you need that written down.
I already put 51F, west breeze, and two juncos at the woodpile. The straight strings are still holding, too.
Do you and Dad want me to pick up the dishwasher part in Spokane? I can front it if the sale ends tomorrow.
That is kind, but wait. After the federal deposits and your dad's old company check, we are close to our usual $4,200 mark before the deductions.
Okay. I was just checking before you put it on the card.
I would rather let the credit-union interest post Friday and then decide. It is small, but I like the notebook to match.
The lodge rate I found is lower if we leave Friday and come back Sunday.
Good. Please do not put it on the card yet. I want to see what is sitting in the marked line after groceries.
I can hold off. Three nights was only $89 more, though.
That $89 would bother me more than the third morning would please me.
Did you catch the library's note about the seed swap? I only saw the top of it before my phone rang.
I saw it at lunch. Saturday, March 21 at 11, bring labeled packets if you have extras.
That works. Anything from the church supper notice yet, or did I imagine that?
It is there. I will look once more after dishes tonight, but right now it only says pies still needed.
I saw your red hat by the boat launch as I drove past. Cold morning for it.
It was crisp but clear. I kept to the flat stretch and came home in about 35 minutes.
That sounds about right. I will bring the muffin tin after lunch.
Do you still need the small cot from church storage for the two little ones?
Yes, please. Brian thinks Friday night might work if his Saturday repair call stays off the board.
I'll bring clean sheets after Bible study. Are you making that apple dessert again?
Yes. Maddie likes to do the topping, and Caleb mostly samples it.
Do you still have that blue carrier in your garage? Nancy at church needs one for her appointment tomorrow.
I gave it away last year with the extra dishes and little blankets. I was glad to have that shelf back.
I will ask Elaine then. Are you setting up your table for muffins Saturday?
Yes. Leonard and I can leave early once the kitchen is wiped down. Nobody here needs us back at noon.
How did you do after the walk by the library this morning?
Mom, the statement photo came through. The clinic posted the March 4 visit twice, but one line should drop off.
Mom, the county page updated the age chart this morning. The green box is the one Dr. Whitcomb's office was probably talking about.
Fine because I did not hurry. I made two rounds, stopped at the bench, then came home and watered the starts.
That helps. I have the paper copy clipped with Leonard's blood pressure card, and I was going to call before I wrote the check.
Thank you. I printed it and put it with Leonard's pillbox note so he sees it before he grumbles.
That sounds like the right amount. Please do the same tomorrow instead of trying to keep up with Marlene.
Good. Ask the pharmacy counter about spacing if they offer both the same week.
Marlene can go ahead if she wants. I am better when I keep my own rhythm.
Mom, are you still doing the library pages tonight and the card table next Thursday? I was checking before I call Sunday.
Good call. Also tell Dad not to lift that wet bag from the garage if his back is acting up.
Yes, Joan and Patrice will be there tonight, and the card table is every other Thursday this month. That is enough running around for me.
I will. I would rather have the timing straight than guess from the TV.
I will. He said he would take it out after supper, but I can split it into two smaller ones.
Fair. You sound better when you keep the same handful of things and do not let everyone add errands onto them.
Marlene already asked if I want coffee after church, so I will save my visiting for that.
Did Dad actually eat lunch today, or just coffee and complaining?
He had a bowl from the vegetable pot, then a small square of tuna casserole. I set the greens aside before he could say there were too many.
Good. That sounds more like a meal than his usual idea.
I saved the rest for tomorrow and put apples on the counter so breakfast is not skipped.
Did you ever call about that dark pickup sitting by the mailboxes, or did it leave?
I used the non-emergency number after supper. I gave the dispatcher the plate and said I did not want anyone rushed at.
That sounds like the right way to do it. Did they give you anything to write down?
Yes, just a call number. I wrote it on the pad by the phone in case Mrs. Nolan asks tomorrow.
Kids cleaned out the school paper drawer. Want the orange and yellow sheets before I toss them?
Save them if it is no trouble. They would make good little spring cutouts for the Tuesday tables.
I can drop them by Sunday. Also found two small yarn balls in Emma's closet.
Those are useful too. I am finishing a few dishcloths tonight, so I will keep everything in the same grocery bag for the center.
Roads should be fine from this side Saturday morning. I will check the pass after work.
Good. Melanie said Sunday would be quieter for her, so Saturday is better for your crew anyway.
I will ask Jen what time the little ones can handle after soccer.
Tell them Grandma saved the oatmeal cookies, and Leonard can show you the loose porch rail.
I am by the bank. Do you need me to wait or are you bringing those envelopes yourself?
Wait five minutes, please. I have the March slips clipped behind the song books and the jar money counted.
I'll stay parked on the side street. Roads are dry.
Thank you. After that I need to stop for flour and apples before Marlene starts setting tables tomorrow.
Before you sit down, can you tell me if you locked the shop door? I looked once but cannot leave it alone tonight.
It is locked. I checked it when I brought in the drill.
All right. I am turning the news off and working on Caleb's scarf instead of going back outside.
Good. Door is locked. Scarf sounds better.
I put that old photo of Mom's blue canner where everyone can see it. Did you find it?
Not until I opened the thing with the little square pictures. I forget it is even on my phone most weeks.
There was a spicy thread under the library levy notice too. I almost tagged you, then thought better of it.
Thank you. I can read a notice without climbing into the basement underneath it.
Mom, Kootenai Heart has a 9:40 opening on March 24. If you take it, leave extra time because parking fills fast.
Please hold it for us. I will put gas money aside this week and keep that whole morning clear.
Bring the blue folder and Leonard's card. I can look over the statement afterward if anything seems odd.
Thank you. I will check the pass report the night before and move the grocery list to Wednesday so Thursday is not crowded.
If you send me a photo of that clinic statement, I can tell you whether the adjustment looks right.
Thank you. It is in Leonard's green folder, behind the January page. I will pull it after I finish clipping the donation slips for Elaine.
That works. Keep the little explanation page with it too, because those offices sometimes split the charge.
I paper-clipped the page to the statement so it won't wander off.
Kids asked if Grandma is making the apple thing when we come up next weekend.
If the roads behave, yes. I wrote down the pan size they liked last time so I do not make it too shallow.
They remember the crunchy top more than anything. I can bring vanilla ice cream.
That would help. I may send you home with a few typed pages too, if I get the family stories matched with the kitchen parts.
I found the file marked deed, insurance, and taxes. It was behind your shop receipts.
Good. Keep the county paper with it. We should not have to dig for that every spring.
I put it in the safe box. I also left the lunch dishes for when you come in.
Be in soon. I am only tightening the gate latch.
Coffee Tuesday still works? I am skipping the quilt shop this month after that dentist bill.
Tuesday works. I did the same with new curtains. We had to keep that little extra line from getting too thin.
That is sensible. I would rather drink coffee at your table than buy fabric I do not need.
I will make muffins and leave the errands for Wednesday when Leonard is already going in.
Do you still want to ride with me to the candidate breakfast at the grange hall?
Yes. I want to hear who will protect the senior-center grant without just asking homeowners for more every time.
Sara Bell is supposed to speak too. I remember you liked how she handled the food-pantry paperwork last winter.
I did. I do not agree with every flyer that comes in my mailbox, but I trust a person who keeps a small office fair and tidy.
Do you still want me to ride with you after the church cleanup, or are you saving that town trip for Wednesday?
Wednesday is better. I can do the refill, bank, and glasses shop in one loop and not spend gas twice.
That makes sense. I can bring the muffin tin Sunday, and you can keep your town money for the errands.
Thank you. I tucked the travel cash away this morning, so I am trying not to borrow from it for little stops.
Do you still want me to pick up the soup cans for Sunday, or are you watching the grocery line pretty closely this week?
I can still do them. I am trying to keep March between $2,700 and $3,000 after that big February folder.
That makes sense. The heat man coming right after the cold snap was poor timing.
It was, but the house is warm and Leonard stopped listening for every little rattle.
I almost called, then remembered you and Leonard had already had your six o'clock program and you try to keep the later part of the night quiet.
That is all right. We watched together, then I set the phone in the kitchen.
Good. Take that Jan Karon book to bed and leave the harder things for morning.
I will. The chapter is marked and the kettle is off.
Mom, are you planting anything yet or just doing your usual cup-of-coffee inspection?
Just looking. The soil still clumps cold in my hand. The geese were noisy enough to make up for no planting.
That sounds like March there. Did Dad ever call the county about the trees by the lane?
He will Monday. I only want the unsafe ones marked, not the whole row taken. Men around here fed children doing that work, so I try not to be foolish about it.
Mom, for Tuesday's nurse check, bring the little home log and the card from your purse. It helps them match everything quickly.
I have the card tucked behind my insurance cards. I wrote down the morning numbers like she asked.
Good. Also take your roomy shoes if you plan to walk the store after.
I will. I have been doing the kitchen stretches before breakfast so the aisles go easier.
When you talk to the billing office Monday, have last month's bank page handy. They may ask what comes in regularly.
I set it beside Leonard's pill list. It shows the two Social Security deposits and his pension, then the Visa payment going out in full.
That should be enough. Don't overpack the folder unless they specifically ask.
I won't. There are no student papers anymore, and the pickup is ours outright, so the folder is thinner than it used to be.
I saw your missed call. Did you need me to read the bottle directions again?
No emergency. I took one acetaminophen after church and wanted to be sure I was not mixing it too close to the other one from last night.
Spacing them out is the right instinct. Write down the times and do not let Dad talk you into taking extras just because the stairs were rude today.
I wrote it on the pad by the phone. The baby sweater can wait until tomorrow when my hands are steadier.
Did Linda make it back north all right after coffee?
Yes, she texted from Sandpoint at 1:40. We talked longer than planned, so I sent the lemon bars with her.
Good. Dad said you were still trying to get Carl on the phone.
I left a message. Montana numbers always make me wonder if I caught him out doing errands.
We came through on 41 and that patched stretch by the grange is rough again. Kids noticed it from the back seat.
I wrote that one down after church. Same week the tax notice arrived, so I want numbers before I say much.
Makes sense. The fire hall pancake sign is up too, by the way.
We will stop after groceries. If they are buying hose or radios, I would rather hand them money where I can see it.
At Miller's. Need anything besides milk?
Small bag of Epsom salt if it's not dear, and another jar of honey. I used the last in tea this morning.
Got it. Those chocolate crinkle cookies for church still on the counter?
Most are. I moved them to the porch before I kept fixing the uneven rows.
Martha's anniversary lunch is the 22nd. She asked if you want the toast pour or the fizzy apple one.
The fizzy apple one, please. I only take the real toast sip on big family days.
I'll tell her. Also, Jerry said people may gather by the back steps after lunch, so we can use the front exit.
Front exit sounds better. My coat won't carry home that smell.
If I come through after coffee, will you be outside or still in the kitchen?
Outside a little before eleven if it warms like they said. I want to tuck spinach seed into the last open line.
Bring your pencil. I saw three robins by the Sandpoint library yesterday, damp and gray, and thought of your porch notes.
I will write yours under town library, rain, and first week they showed up. Those rows out back are finally behaving.
I found two old clippings in Mom's recipe box, one about the mill fire and one with the school bus picture.
Could you bring them when you come for coffee Friday? The library packet had that same school bus route mentioned.
Sure. I will put them in a folder so they do not get bent.
Perfect. We can look at them at the kitchen table and I will copy only the names I need.
I can take the muffin sign if you want. You already have the birthday table, prize basket, and book cart this week.
Please do. I counted it up and I am already at about nine hours before Saturday's luncheon setup.
Then let me take the sign and the napkins. You do plenty, and nobody needs you wearing yourself thin.
I can come by after muffins are in the oven if you want another set of eyes on that packet.
Thank you. I will handle the center tables Friday and keep Thursday for the library cart.
Do you still want me to bring the spring tablecloths on Friday, or did you find enough in that blue tub?
That would help. I tucked the March page in Leonard's folder, but the loose slips keep sliding behind the calendar by the phone.
Bring four if you can. I found the name tags from 2021 tucked behind the bingo cards, so at least that part is settled.
I can also call Eileen about the dessert pan. You have enough calls on your list already.
I will bring clips. Is this for the Spokane drive or the Coeur d'Alene one?
Spokane. I put a phone reminder for the noon call too, in case they change the time again.
Thank you. If she says yes, I will mark her beside cleanup instead of serving.
Kids want to bring sleeping bags if we come Sunday. Roads look okay so far.
That works. I will move the ironing board out of the back room and make space on the floor.
Need us to bring anything besides apple juice?
Only yourselves. I like being able to put the house back quiet after company leaves.
Did my shop check land yet?
Yes. Yours is in, the two Treasury ones are in, and the credit union added $11.37.
Enough for groceries and propane then?
Yes, as long as I keep the before-takeout number near $4,200 and do not forget the premiums.
Coffee after the library talk Tuesday? They said the county table will have those incident-card forms.
Yes. I want one for the folder, same as keeping doctor receipts and repair invoices.
You and your folders. Want me to save you a seat near the aisle?
Please. I also want to ask whether the non-emergency call numbers can be looked up later.
Do you still want me to ride along after Bible study, or did Leonard decide the errand was unnecessary?
He is calling it fussing, but Dr. Whitcomb's nurse and the pharmacy both said not to put it off too long.
Then I will bring my car around at 11:15. We can stop for milk afterward.
I can finish tying the tags on the church dishcloths if your hands have had enough tonight.
That would be kind. I managed six rows, then put the needles down and used the warm pack.
Good. Bring the basket Sunday and let me carry it in. Those front steps are not worth being brave over.
Thank you. I am leaving the ibuprofen alone tonight unless I truly need it.
At Miller's. They have that sleep candy the neighbor mentioned on end cap.
Leave it there. Chamomile tea is enough for me.
Need anything for tomorrow lunch?
Just sparkling apple bottles and mints. I am keeping it simple.
I sent the bake sale flyer the way Ruth asked, but I can also text it if that is easier.
Text is easiest. Those public pages make me hunt around too much.
Someone turned the parking vote notice into a quarrel again.
Then I will just bring muffins and keep my sentence out of that pile.
Mom, when you type the tomato page, can you include whether you used the small purple ones or the striped ones?
Striped, roasted with basil after church. I found the margin note where I wrote 'less oil' from last August.
Perfect. The kids will like the little notes in your voice.
I am tucking a short story beside that one, about your grandpa carrying tomato baskets in the old pickup.
Coffee Tuesday? I saved the little voter card from the Sandpoint paper for you.
Tuesday works. Bring it along. I like comparing who talks about spending carefully and who only promises new things.
You may surprise Leonard on one of those town offices.
Maybe. For county and town jobs I look at who has actually shown up, returned calls, and treated people square.
Did Ruth press you again about the May program after church?
She did. I said I can bake and make six phone calls, but I am leaving the first page for someone else's handwriting.
That sounds right. You already have the center on Tuesday, and Thursday too when they ask.
Carol laughed and said she would sit by me tomorrow so I do not erase her name from the card boxes.
Maddie wore the blue hat to school. Sara sent you a picture.
I saw it and sent Sara a little note back for Maddie. Caleb's baseball card went in today's mail.
Good timing. Also, April 11 is probably too tight with games, but maybe the first clear Saturday after that.
We will keep it loose. Spring roads and ball schedules can decide for us.
Did that small county thing turn out all right? I saw a reminder at work and thought of you.
Yes, we went when the sun came through. I kept the stub with the tax papers for now.
Of course you did. You keep better records than half the front desk.
It keeps me from forgetting the little ones. They come around quietly.
I'm going by the shed. Do you still need that folding chair rack pulled out?
Yes, please. I also set the blue bag by the back door with the yarn needles, extra greeting cards, and the little blankets.
Want me to put it all in the car before I start the mower?
That would help. I promised Alice I would have everything there before 12:30 so nobody has to hunt for supplies.
I'm at Yoke's. Do we need crackers for soup?
Unsalted ones if they have them. I already did my after-lunch tablet and marked the Wednesday square.
Found them. Your refill bag is in the truck console too.
Thank you. I will check it against the purse card before I put it in Sunday's row.
You sent that muffin recipe before sunrise. Were you already up with your notebook?
Since a little after four. I wrote down the bake sale calls, then checked the freezer bags twice like that would change anything.
Bring the notebook to coffee and we will cross off half of it. I can call Aunt Ruth for you.
That helps. I will walk first and put the yarn in my bag so my hands have something useful to do.
Coffee Friday still good? I can bring back that folder you left in my car.
Friday is good. Is it the 2025 one with Elaine's sticky note on the front?
Yes. It has the yellow tab and a few garden receipts tucked in the side pocket.
That is the one. I need to file it back beside 2024 and then copy the seed totals into my garden notebook.
Mom, I saw a paperback at the hospital sale with a train station on the cover. Want me to hold it for you?
Maybe, if it is not too thick. I already have April's library copy waiting and I like to finish the one they choose first.
That sounds like you. I will skip it unless it is a dollar.
A dollar is fine. Otherwise I will stay with the library stack and my Tuesday notes.
Roads look clear Saturday. Want us to bring anything, or are you already stocked?
I planned chili and cornbread, so just bring the kids' coats. I checked the pantry list this morning.
Sounds good. Dad still messing with that mower, or should I bring my socket set?
He says he has it, after he finishes the driveway edges. I put the tax papers away so the table is clear.
Fog is thick by the highway. You still going into town?
I will wait until it lifts. The center list is ready, and Mr. Ellison knows where the coffee cans are if I am late.
Good. Don't take on that extra May thing on top of it.
I already kept my answer small: pies and two calls. Carol has the Thursday tally sheets in her purse.
I put the rake by the back steps. Ground is soft enough.
Thank you. I will do one bed, take my tea on the porch, then decide about the second.
Good. Leave the heavy bag for me.
I will. After that I may walk to the mailbox and back before breakfast, nothing more.
At the bank. Want me to get a printout for the folder?
Yes, just March. It should show the Visa cleared, the county tax check, and our regular deposits.
Do they need anything on the house or pickup?
No, I have the title copies at home, and the house page only has our names on it. Nothing else to add to that packet.
Are you out by the lake already or did that wind keep you home?
Out there now. I stayed on the sheltered side and will turn back at the bench.
Good. Coffee at ten still works if your legs are not tired.
Ten works. I am back, and it was the same easy 35 or so.
Did your Thursday crowd finish on time, or did the speaker run long again?
We finished by 1:25. I gave him the five-minute card and had Ruth start the coffee cups while I gathered the ride slips.
That sounds like you. Do you still keep the old pencil note in the binder from when you first took over the sign-up table?
I do. It is faded now, but it still reminds me where the room key and receipt pouch belong.
Kids asked if Grandma's molasses cookies survived the drive tomorrow.
They are in the tin already. I put soup on low and made tea, so I am staying out of that tin.
Good plan. Roads look fine from here.
I'll send some broth home with you too, if Leonard doesn't claim it first.
Kids asked if you and Dad are still doing that Idaho weekend. They want postcards.
Kids wanted to FaceTime but I told them Grandpa's chair time with you is right now.
If the April 3 move finishes it, yes. I have Sun Valley written on the envelope already.
You remembered. We are settled in with our trays, so after 6:40 would be better.
You could just stay longer while you are there.
No, two sleeps is the right size for us. Any more and I would be doing sums instead of looking around.
No rush. Also don't read comments tonight about that Spokane story. It was a mess.
I won't. I have the paperback Linda loaned me on the nightstand.
Kids are asking about coming up Sunday. Weather app says freezing rain early near Rathdrum.
Let us decide Saturday evening. I have chili and bread in the freezer, so nobody has to stop twice if the roads are only fair.
That works. I can bring the bracket for Dad's shelf if we make it.
Good. I kept a little back from this week's cash in case that shelf needs screws or a board while you are here.
Kids' braces quote came in and I had to sit down. You ever split a surprise bill over a couple paydays?
Yes. We had that $400 heater piece and I marked two $50 returns on the calendar so the cushion is not left low.
That makes sense. I am trying to keep ours from getting wiped out all at once.
One small step at a time is easier than waiting for a big amount.
I left the assessor envelope by your chair. Same pile as the fire hall raffle tickets.
Thank you. I want to look at the line changes before Monday. Also remind me to call the library about the levy postcard.
You want me to take the cans to church Sunday or wait?
Take them Sunday, please. And if the senior bus sheet is still on the bulletin board, bring me one.
News is starting. They are talking about that state budget piece again.
I am coming in. I want to hear whether they cut anything before asking families to cover more.
Your ballot envelope is on the counter too.
Leave it there, please. I still want to read Sara's answers one more time before I seal it.
If I stop after Sandpoint, can I bring those two bags of hand-me-down books for your church table?
Yes, leave them by the hall bench. The spare closet is finally neat since Melanie's old boxes went to her.
Do you want the small automatic feeder I found in my pantry, or should I donate it too?
Donate it. I am keeping our mornings simple, just coffee, Leonard's toast, and my list.
I may come through after Sandpoint if the rain lets up. Need me to bring anything from Yoke's?
Maybe just apples if they look decent. I have oats, beans, tuna, and two cans of tomatoes here already.
I can grab apples. Coffee at your table if I make it before noon?
Yes. I will have a salad washed and maybe soup warming, depending how much talking we do.
Coffee Monday still good? I can come through after my dentist.
Monday works. I have no office place to be, just the center calendar to finish and two carts waiting at the library later in the week.
Good. I will bring those canning notes too. Are you keeping Saturday free after the luncheon?
Mostly. March has been closer to twelve hours with the luncheon, so I am leaving the rest of Saturday quiet.
I can stop in Spirit Lake after my Sandpoint appointment if you need help moving that cedar chest.
Thank you, but Leonard says he can slide it with the dolly. I only need you to help me sort the old envelopes.
I want to see the one from when you two were so young. Mom kept talking about your blue dress.
It is still in there with the county papers and the little cake knife. Come after 2:00 and I will put coffee on.
If I come through Sunday, do you want those bean seeds from Sandpoint? Mine are sitting on the counter.
Yes, bring them. The lower bed finally smells right after that rain, and I want them in before the next cold snap.
I saw trucks stacked by the north road again. Reminded me of Dad coming home with pitch on his cuffs.
I remember. I still hate seeing a bare slope, but I know what those paychecks did for supper tables.
Snow is sticking by Careywood. I am not keen on the last stretch tonight.
Then stay put here. Leonard already moved the laundry basket out of the small room.
Thank him for me. I can head back to Sandpoint after breakfast if it clears.
That works. I will also give you Carl's address card so it does not sit on my counter another week.
I may come through Tuesday for coffee if the roads stay dry. Need anything from Sandpoint?
Just bring yourself. I put the April cash in the little sleeves today, so I am leaving the drugstore and tire place alone until the first.
You are more patient than I am. I still need to sort the receipt from my eye exam before I forget where I put it.
Bring it if you want. Melanie showed me to circle the amount they actually want, then wait a week if the paper looks odd.
Are you still all right bringing muffins Sunday, or should I put Helen down instead?
I can bring them. I waited until the last March deposits cleared before buying walnuts, so I am not guessing.
That sounds like you. I will leave you on the list for two dozen.
Thank you. Once Leonard's check and those two government entries are written in, the notebook comes out around the same $4,200 before the little things are pulled away.
For the women's supper, June put you next to the coffee urn again. She remembered you like a clear table.
Patrice asked if you wanted to join the luncheon table on Tuesday after the library returns.
That is kind of her. Coffee and lemon water suit me fine.
Please tell her thank you, but I will just do the returns and come home. I have you Sunday, Joan on the 31st, and that is plenty.
Someone left a small packet in the church kitchen drawer after the last rental. I am putting it in the office lost-and-found, not near the food.
Thank you. I would rather not handle it, especially while setting out muffins.
I will tell her. I saved two muffins for Sunday, and we can sit in the kitchen after service if Leonard does not need you right away.
That sounds just right. I would rather have a quiet visit I can count on than squeeze in another table.
The Coeur d'Alene office called back. They moved Dad to 10:40 on Tuesday, not 11:15.
I just changed the kitchen square and the phone alert. I will put the new slip in his green folder before supper.
Good. Take the small pill list too, since they asked what changed since February.
It is already clipped to the inside flap. We will leave early enough to miss the worst of 95.
Mom, are you still doing those forms tonight? You sounded tired after the potluck.
Just finishing the month-end report. The last two apple pans were gone before coffee was poured, so at least I did not bring leftovers home.
Please eat something besides crumbs and coffee. Can the report wait until morning?
I put up the two Coeur d'Alene photos from Anna's concert. No need to answer there, just wanted you to see them.
I will finish the totals, set the bulletin list in my purse for Sunday, and then have soup.
I will see them after supper. I already looked this morning for the senior-center lunch time and the church list.
That sounds about right for you. Dad said you also knew about the library closing before the radio mentioned it.
The library note was right above the Spirit Lake road update, and below that someone up north posted about covering seedlings tonight.
Are you still up for coffee Monday, or did the house bills make you want to stay put?
Coffee is fine. March is landing just under $3,000 if nothing odd happens before Tuesday.
Good. That $3,400 page from February sounded like enough excitement for one winter.
Exactly. I am glad we paid the heating man and can go back to ordinary receipts.
After lunch I will wait for Melanie's call before starting the roast. Can you bring in the photo packet from Brian's last stop?
Got it. The packet with Jen and the two school pictures?
Yes. I want to compare sizes before mailing Melanie hers.
On the table. I also put your Coeur d'Alene note with it.
I can drop the muffin tin after church supper. Would that be too late?
That is fine. I am going out around six-thirty to give the peas a drink and pull the crooked marker before it bothers me another day.
I smiled at that. Bring your porch notebook if the evening birds are making a show.
I will. Yesterday was 58F, clear, two swallows over the church parking lot, and I want to see if they pass the ditch tonight.
